# `silk/crypto/sm4`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Encrypt with the SM4 block cipher (GB/T 32907-2016, ISO/IEC 18033-3).

## When to use
Use [`Sm4`](#Sm4) when a format names SM4, such as `sm4-cbc` or `sm4-ctr` in OpenSSL or Node.js. Run
it in a mode from `silk.crypto.block_cipher`, such as `Cbc<Sm4>`.

## Details
The key and the block are 16 bytes, and there are 32 rounds. [`Sm4`](#Sm4) conforms to `BlockCipher`.
Nothing allocates.

## Gotchas
The S-box is a table lookup, so the time of a block can depend on the key and the data through
the cache, as in OpenSSL's portable code. The value holds key material and is not erased when it
is dropped.

## Examples
### Encrypt one block
```silk
import silk.crypto.block_cipher { BlockCipher, BlockCipherError }
import silk.crypto.sm4 { Sm4 }
import silk.core.result { Result }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // The example of GB/T 32907-2016 appendix A.
  let key: [u8; 16] = [0x01, 0x23, 0x45, 0x67, 0x89, 0xab, 0xcd, 0xef, 0xfe, 0xdc, 0xba, 0x98, 0x76, 0x54, 0x32, 0x10]
  let cipher = match Sm4.make(&key) {
    Result<Sm4, BlockCipherError>.Success { value } => move value
    Result<Sm4, BlockCipherError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let mut block = key
  cipher.encryptBlock(&mut block)
  if block[0] != 0x68 || block[1] != 0x1e || block[15] != 0x46 {
    return 1
  }
  cipher.decryptBlock(&mut block)
  if block[0] != 0x01 || block[15] != 0x10 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Sm4` with `import silk.crypto.sm4 { Sm4 }`.

## `Sm4`

```silk
pub struct Sm4
```

An SM4 key schedule.

### Details

Make one with [`Sm4.make`](#Sm4.impl.make) and run it in a mode from `silk.crypto.block_cipher`, or call
`encryptBlock` and `decryptBlock` of `BlockCipher` on one 16-byte block.
